title: Computer Based Office Admin and Organization
overview: Modern office administration depends on the ability to organize information, documents, communication, schedules, records, and routine workflows efficiently through digital tools. Administrative professionals are increasingly expected to combine strong organizational skills with confident use of computer-based systems to support managers, teams, customers, and daily business operations.

This practical course develops the essential digital and organizational competencies required for effective office administration. Participants will learn how to structure electronic files, manage documents and correspondence, organize email and calendars, prepare professional office documents, work with basic data and tracking tools, coordinate meetings, maintain records, and improve the flow of routine administrative work.

The program emphasizes practical application rather than software theory. Participants will work through realistic office tasks using common productivity applications and learn how to create consistent systems for naming, storing, retrieving, updating, sharing, and protecting information. The course also addresses prioritization, confidentiality, workflow control, and administrative quality standards.

By the end of the program, participants will be able to organize a more efficient computer-based office environment and apply practical systems that improve accuracy, accessibility, communication, follow-up, and productivity.
audience: Administrative assistants, executive secretaries, office administrators, coordinators, reception and front-office staff, personal assistants, document controllers, junior administrative employees, and professionals whose roles involve computer-based office organization, correspondence, scheduling, records, documentation, and administrative support.
methodology: The course uses a hands-on methodology combining short demonstrations with guided computer practice, individual exercises, office simulations, document-production tasks, file-management activities, email and calendar exercises, spreadsheet-based tracking activities, case studies, and workflow improvement exercises. Participants will work with realistic administrative scenarios and create practical templates, filing structures, trackers, and organizational systems that can be adapted to their workplace.
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Organize a structured and efficient computer-based office environment.
Create logical electronic filing systems that support fast storage and retrieval of information.
Apply consistent file-naming, version-control, and document-management practices.
Prepare and format professional office documents and routine business correspondence.
Manage email, contacts, calendars, appointments, and meeting schedules more effectively.
Use spreadsheets and simple digital trackers to organize administrative information and follow-up.
Coordinate meetings and maintain the related digital documentation.
Apply practical methods for organizing tasks, deadlines, reminders, and recurring administrative work.
Protect confidential information and apply appropriate access, sharing, backup, and retention practices.
Develop practical improvements for the organization and efficiency of their own administrative workflow.
